interactions.summary: Students work through the siren dream with Jiang, who keeps pressing the paradox that Beatrice addresses Virgil instead of Dante until the class lands on the claim that, inside the dream, Dante has become Virgil.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang-led interpretive exchange with several student answers.

claims.claim: A student suggests the dream scene warns Dante not to become stillborn inside Virgil and reads the siren as a love left to fester and rot.
Jiang treats the paradox of Beatrice speaking to Virgil inside Dante's dream as evidence that the dream is collapsing Dante and Virgil into one another.
The student formulation Jiang endorses is that the dream says Dante is Virgil, which makes the siren scene a warning about identification with the guide.

signature_moments.moment: The interpretive breakthrough is the blunt sentence that inside the dream Dante is Virgil.
signature_moments.source_phrase: So in this dream, Dante is Virgil
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It converts a strange staging detail into the key warning of the whole dream sequence.

signature_moments.moment: The siren's exposed belly becomes an image of love gone rotten or stillborn inside the paternal guide.
signature_moments.source_phrase: please don't get stillborn in Virgil
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is one of the class's most vivid attempts to translate dream image into moral diagnosis.

chronology_notes.note: This packet develops the June 26 Virgil-as-siren hypothesis into a stronger identity claim: Dante's dream shows him becoming Virgil.

uncertainty_notes.note: The stillbirth/rotting-baby reading is a student's speculative extension of the image, not a settled Jiang claim.
